newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian death squad massacres 30 villagers.
newsitem.headline: Colombian death squad massacres 30 villagers.

text.p: A right-wing death squad massacred about 30 people in a remote village of eastern Colombia, Red Cross and local officials said on Monday.
The attack took place in Mapiripan in Meta province over the weekend but Teddy Torbeaum, head of the Red Cross in Meta province, told Reuters the final death toll was not yet clear.

"I met the mayor of Mapiripan this morning and he told me that at least 30 people had been massacred. But we will not know exactly how many dead there are until we can recover the corpes," Torbeaum said in a telephone interview.

Police and army troops flew to Mapiripan aboard five helicopters on Monday but declined to give details of the number of dead and the circumstances of the massacre until they had toured the village of about 1,000 people and the surrounding countryside.

"This paramilitary gang has been coming in and out of the village for the last week. Then yesterday they began killing people...," municipal council employee Luis Prieto said by phone. "At least 25 or 30 people have died but we have not been able to go out into the rural area near the village to check."

In an interview with the Radionet radio network, provincial Gov. Alfonso Ortiz said witnesses told him several of the victims had been beheaded and that one head was left at the doors of the village medical post.

Sketchy witness reports said a gang of about 100 paramilitary fighters entered the village, killing three people in the square and dragging others off to more isolated areas before murdering them, he said.
"These people were dressed in uniforms like the army and were armed to the teeth," villager Susana Perez said by phone. "They had pistols, machine guns and knives. Everybody here was terrified."

Right-wing death squads, which call themselves self-defence groups, frequently target those they suspect of being leftist rebel sympathisers. Ortiz said guerrilla groups had traditionally had a strong presence in the area.
"The presence of the state in the zone is zero ... narco-traffickers and guerrillas have control of the region," he said.
Red Cross officials said hundreds of villagers, fearing further violence, had fled on foot, by plane and by river.
Mapiripan is on the banks of the Guaviare River, which divides Meta and Guaviare provinces.
The residents are mostly poor peasants who grow plantain, yucca, beans, maize and sorghum. Some also tend illicit farms of coca leaf, the raw material for cocaine.
News of the massacre came a day after President Ernesto Samper promised a widespread crackdown on both leftist guerrillas and paramilitary gangs.

In his speech to inaugurate a session of Congress he also firmed up his plans for a new peace process to end the country's three-decade-old guerrilla war and said paramilitary groups would be invited to take part in the dialogue.
If the number of dead is confirmed it will be one of the worst massacre since January 1994 when 35 people were slain by leftist guerrillas at a party in the town of Apartado in Uraba.
